item.title: Open for business in Pensacola
item.description: Following the news that American Magic (USA) would not compete in the 38th edition of the America’s Cup, the two-time challenger has turned their focus on the American Magic High Performance Center (AMHPC) in Pensacola, Florida. Located in the Port of Pensacola, the facility provides a world-class sailing and performance platform in the United States. item.title: Change of helm at Quantum Sails
item.description: Quantum Sails has promoted Andrew Scott in the position of President, effective January 1, 2026. Ed Reynolds, President since 2007, has been associated with Quantum Sails since 1996. - Full report

item.title: 49erFX: World’s Coolest Yachts
item.description: Yachting World has been asking top sailors and marine industry gurus to choose the coolest and most innovative yachts of our times, and Olympian Francesca Clapcich nominated the 49erFX dinghy. item.title: Two teams, One Jules Verne Trophy
item.description: The Jules Verne Trophy is awarded for the fastest time around the world by any type of yacht with no restrictions on the size of the crew, starting and finishing from the exact line between the Le Créac’h Lighthouse off the eastern tip of France and the southernmost point of England. It was first won in 1993, with all nine winners as either catamarans or trimarans. item.title: Countdown to 38th Puerto Vallarta Race
item.description: Twenty-six boats from across the USA and Australia are entered to compete in the biennial San Diego to Puerto Vallarta race, with staggered starts on February 26, 27, and 28. As the dominant offshore race for 2026, completing the 1000 nm course earns competitors margaritas, mariachi bands, and the warm welcome of Mainland Mexico. - Full report

item.title: Knockout stage begins at Tour Finals
item.description: The qualifying phase of the 2025 World Match Racing Tour Final has eliminated half the field as eight teams advance to the knockout stage, with racing in Far East 28Rs being held January 6-11, 2026 in Shenzhen, China. Nick Egnot-Johnson (NZL), Jeppe Borch (DEN), Chris Poole (USA), Aurélien Pierroz (FRA), Ian Williams (GBR), Cole Tapper (AUS), Oscar Engström (SWE), and Timothée Rossi (FRA) will continue to vie for the Match Racing World Champion title and a share of the USD200,000 prize purse. -
